failedAssertions.reason: Did not observe forced SIGKILL path with confirmed process termination.
With tier port 8101 occupied, startup did not emit `Port ... already in use by PID ...`; it attempted tier launch and later reported health-check timeout instead of explicit port-owner detection.

blockedAssertions.blockedBy: End-to-end first-time journey is blocked in this milestone because `mlx-stack pull` is not implemented (`Not yet implemented. Coming in the pull-command feature.`), so required model acquisition step cannot be executed.

Config propagation was confirmed for `litellm-port` (up/status on 5000), `memory-budget-pct` (recommend/init budget 76.8 GB), and `model-dir` (models command used custom directory), but validation of `default-quant -> pull` and `model-dir -> pull` could not be completed because `mlx-stack pull` is currently a placeholder (`Not yet implemented`).

Profile/recommend/init flow, schema_version rejection, and `vllm_flags -> up --dry-run` translation were validated, but full cross-command data consistency could not be completed because `bench --save` and `pull` are placeholder commands and do not create benchmark/models inventory artifacts required by the assertion.

Tier-start behavior requiring running services could not be validated because no local model files exist in isolated MLX_STACK_HOME; command consistently skipped fast tier with pull instruction. Invalid-tier error path was validated.

frictions.description: Using UV_INDEX_URL to force dependency-install failure broke outer 'uv run' resolution before mlx-stack executed.
frictions.resolution: Switched to a local uv shim for inner dependency-install failure simulation while keeping outer '/opt/homebrew/bin/uv run' intact.

frictions.description: uv emitted a non-fatal warning about malformed tool 'bin' when using a nested UV_TOOL_DIR path.
frictions.resolution: Warning did not affect installs; proceeded and verified binaries in isolated tool bin.

frictions.description: Environment had litellm version mismatch warning (installed v1.82.6 vs pinned v1.67.2) printed on each up run.
frictions.resolution: Warning was non-blocking for assigned startup-flow assertions; proceeded with isolated shim-backed startup checks.

frictions.description: Port-conflict simulation required a longer timeout because startup attempted to launch on the occupied port and only failed after health-check timeout, rather than immediate conflict skip.
frictions.resolution: Increased test command timeout to allow full failure path completion and captured explicit timeout behavior for assertion adjudication.

frictions.description: Dependency check emits non-blocking litellm version mismatch warning on each up run (installed v1.82.6 vs pinned v1.67.2).
frictions.resolution: Treated warning as informational and proceeded because it did not prevent exercising assigned lifecycle assertions.

frictions.description: Dedicated flow-validator subagent for this group returned an insufficient-permission error twice.
frictions.resolution: Executed the assigned down-flow assertions directly in validator session with strict MLX_STACK_HOME isolation and captured evidence artifacts.

frictions.description: Initial init invocation failed because PATH omitted /usr/sbin, so sysctl lookup failed during hardware detection.
frictions.resolution: Re-ran commands with system path entries (/usr/sbin:/sbin) included in PATH.

frictions.description: Python http.server-based shim responders were non-responsive in this environment for health checks, causing false down states.
frictions.resolution: Replaced isolation-only shim implementations with socket-based HTTP responders and re-ran all affected status lifecycle checks.

frictions.description: litellm version mismatch warning (`installed v1.82.6, expected v1.67.2`) appears on lifecycle runs and adds noise to startup output.
frictions.resolution: Treated as non-blocking because assertions are cross-flow behavior checks and startup still completed successfully.

dedupedBlockers: No local model artifacts were present in isolated MLX_STACK_HOME, so 'up --tier fast' skipped service startup and LiteLLM never started.
pull command unavailable in current milestone blocks full first-time journey validation.
`mlx-stack pull` is not implemented in this build, blocking end-to-end validation of default-quant/model-dir propagation into actual downloads.
`mlx-stack bench --save` is not implemented in this build, blocking validation that benchmark artifacts are consumed across commands for data consistency.
